_authority: This file is the authority on accredited time. hours/GUIDE.md points at it and must not restate these numbers in prose.

academic_hour.rule: Read the minute value from the approved programme itself. Never assume 60.
academic_hour.on_absence: UNKNOWN - ask the operator, do not guess. Every downstream number depends on it.

budget.rule: built_minutes == allocated_minutes, exactly, per module and in total
budget.why_zero: A tolerance is a licence to drift. GAS BASIC drifted 535 min because nothing counted.

overflow.rule: Class time is fixed by the programme. Content that will not fit is moved to the handout, never squeezed into the minutes and never silently cut.
overflow.must_record: every item moved, with its source topic, in the companion file

underrun.rule: Also a defect. A module that teaches 120 min against 160 allocated is under-delivering an accredited hour and the operator must be told.

scope.modules_only: Topics whose hours sit outside the modules are excluded from the module budget. On GAS BASIC that is the final assessment (topic 23, 2 h), which is separate from every module check.
scope.detect: A topic is outside the modules when no module claims it in the module->topics map. List these explicitly at the gate rather than letting them vanish.

when_unreachable.rule: Deliver the theory hours as active learning - a trainee activity inside the theory block.
when_unreachable.defect: A theory block with no trainee activity in it.
when_unreachable.record: achieved ratio + the reason it is below target, in the companion file

GAS BASIC.note: fixed by the programme's own table - topics 8, 9, 16, 17 carry all 8 practical hours

sub.purpose: re-express to make a topic digital or practical
constraints: marked PROVISIONAL until the owner ratifies
never renumbered in anything a trainee sees

ilo.programme_vs_model_course: The approved programme governs. An IMO model course is guidance and is cited as support, never as authority.

timetable.rule: The programme's own timetable bounds the day. Derive slots from it; do not invent a day shape.
timetable.check: sum(module minutes) + outside-module minutes <= days * slots_per_day * slot_min. If it does not fit, the course cannot be delivered in the accredited days and that is a finding, not a rounding error.
timetable.delivery_days: The days a school SELLS may exceed the days the programme was accredited with. Transcribe days from the programme and NEVER edit it to make a check pass - that falsifies the record the check verifies against. Put the delivered figure in delivery_days. If delivery_days > days, the timetable being run is not the one the accreditation describes and the accreditor must be told: a finding to report, not a number to adjust. GAS BASIC, 2026-09-07: accredited 4 days = 1760 min, built 2100, sold as 5 days = 2200.

one_plan_per_module.rule: Every module carries exactly one plan document that states its allocated and built minutes on its own face.
one_plan_per_module.why: GAS BASIC has no plan for modules 1 and 8 and a differently-marked one for 7, so its timings could not be summed from a single source.
one_plan_per_module.good_example: the M5 plan's own header - '8 academic hours = 320 min | Teaching below: 330 min' - which self-reports the gap where anyone can see it

minutes_live_in.primary: the module plan, as a per-activity figure
minutes_live_in.mirrored_in: START_HERE / the module entry page, as step durations
minutes_live_in.rule: One of these is the source of truth and the other is generated from it. Two hand-maintained copies drift.

course_start_extension.note: COURSE_START.json (owned by novikontas-course-start) has NO hours field. This skill writes an additive block and never alters the existing schema.
